title: Compatible Cohen power-series presentations of a complete local map
statement: Let $f:(A,\mathfrak m_A)\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], both complete for their maximal-ideal-adic topologies [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Then there are complete regular local rings $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$, surjective local maps $q:R\to A$ and $v:S\to B$, and a local map $u:R\to S$ with $vu=fq$, such that $R$ and $S$ are formal power-series rings [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] over fields if $A/\mathfrak m_A$ has characteristic zero and over Cohen rings [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] if it has characteristic $p>0$. One can choose a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $R$ whose images in $S$ extend to a regular system of parameters of $S$, with $t_1=p$ in residue characteristic $p$. The map $R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings), statement and proof; the choice $t_1=p$ is made in the proof of Proposition Tag 07NQ (proposition-fs-flat-fibre-fs)

proof.text: Apply the Cohen power-series presentation theorem to ULift A in Type(max u v), transporting locality, Noetherianity and completeness along the explicit ring equivalence. Compose its surjection with the equivalence back to A. In the field branch the coefficient residue equivalence gives characteristic zero of Lambda_A; in the Cohen branch the source canonical parameters start with p.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN, proof; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NN

proof.text: Apply the canonical-parameter extension lemma to g=f q, with c=0 in the field case and c=p in the Cohen case. It gives the compatible S,v,u and extended parameter list. Transfer the characteristic of k_ULift_A to k_A by the induced injective residue homomorphism. Uniqueness of characteristic proves the two universal coefficient clauses and, in residue characteristic p, the required head of t.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN, proof; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NN

proof.text: Apply the regular-generators theorem to the full list t.map u ++ z. Its weak regularity restricts to t.map u by the append criterion. Every element of that initial list lies in m_S, so the local Nakayama regularity criterion upgrades it to a regular sequence. Apply flat_of_regular_parameters to t, using its length as the dimension and its spanning equality, to get u.Flat.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN, proof; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NN

proof.text: The regular-generators theorem also makes the quotient of S by the first t.length parameters regular local. The take-append identity identifies these parameters with t.map u. Ideal.map_ofList and the spanning equality for t identify this ideal with map u m_R. Transport regularity along that ideal equality. This argument covers the empty initial list.

split_report.summary: Proof in 5 steps following Stacks 07NN (read with 07NL, 07NJ, 032A, 00R4, 00NU and the proof of 07NQ for t_1=p). The lead note asked to cite lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-map-regular-presentation for R, S; its statement does not say that R and S are power-series rings over fields or Cohen rings (that is only in its proof), and a regular complete local ring need not be such a power-series ring (ramified case: p in m^2), so its statement cannot give this node and is not cited (C3: no use of a proof). Instead the construction is done from statements: Cohen presentations of A and B (lem-weil-pbc-cohen-power-series-presentation, which gives t_1=p), the formal-smoothness lift, S = Lambda_B[[Y,Z]] with u(X_i)=phi(X_i)+Y_i, and flatness/fibre from the parameter nodes. Step 4 replaces the regular-presentation node's substitution automorphism by the direct observation that u(t), Z generate m_S and are dim S in number. No new nodes. No slopmaster2 Lean (grep by id, 07NN, Cohen, power series).
